tasks.short: Place requested telephone calls and arrange conference calls.

steps.what: Receive instructions and clarify participants, timing, purpose and contact details.

loop.input: Spoken call request and permitted directory references.
loop.output: Call brief with participants, timing and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields; read back names, numbers and timing to the requester.
loop.stop: One extraction and two clarification attempts; then hand over to the operator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken instructions contain corrections and ambiguous names. Structured requests bypass the loop.

steps.what: Find telephone numbers and resolve ambiguous directory matches.
Coordinate availability and conference details with participants.
Dial the requested destination or launch the conference connection.
Check participants are connected and resolve failed connections.

tasks.design: Configure structured call requests, directory lookup and conference templates in the {TELEPHONY} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded extraction loop drafts spoken requests; existing scheduling features propose times, and the requester confirms destinations before calls or invitations take effect. The operator handles ambiguous identities, unavailable participants and failed connections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine features existed, but spoken instructions, stale directories and cross-company availability left coordination with the operator.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing conference and directory configuration can handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting request forms and adding bounded speech extraction.
tasks.still_hard: External availability, namesakes, accessibility needs and confidential calls still need care. Recording and transcription require a justified GDPR basis and suitable retention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a sensitive call, negotiating an acceptable alternative and calmly reconnecting people.

ambition.what: Assisted conference setup for employees who need accessibility support.

tasks.altitude: The operator spends less time copying numbers and chasing availability, and more time helping difficult connections. No new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Coordinate accessible remote attendance for visitors.
reach.learn: Accessibility preferences, visitor protocols and supported connection options.
Basic call diagnostics and the support escalation checklist.

evidence.claim: Configured spoken directory lookup can return multiple matches and distinguish namesakes by department.
Structured requests, availability checks and conference templates can reduce routine coordination; the proposed savings are estimates.
An AI voice interface needs caller disclosure and applicable synthetic-audio marking.

assumptions: The baseline is an operator arranging calls for staff in a mid-size European company.
Immediate calls skip availability coordination; conference requests use the full sequence.
Time shares describe a mixed workload, not time spent on every individual request.
The spoken-request loop is optional; structured requests use deterministic processing.
Effort ranges cover a small rollout using existing infrastructure. Consultation may add elapsed time.
unknowns: Which directory, scheduling and call-control interfaces are available?
How many requests arrive verbally rather than through structured channels?
Can requesters approve participant lists through an existing interface?
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How reliably do current directory searches resolve local names and namesakes?
Which failures require operator judgement rather than a standard retry?
Can the speech service meet disclosure, retention and access requirements without retaining recordings?
new_work: Review unclear call briefs and unresolved directory matches.
Maintain conference templates and escalation routes.
Check failed connections and integration errors.
Maintain disclosure wording and transcription retention settings.

tasks.short: Receive, sort, record and dispatch physical mail, parcels and deliveries.

steps.what: Receive deliveries and inspect packaging, labels and visible damage.
Sort incoming items by recipient, location and handling requirements.
Enter tracked items and recipient details in the delivery register.
Notify recipients that their tracked delivery is ready for collection.
Create postage labels in the {OTHER} postal booking system.
Pack outgoing items and attach the checked postage label.
Hand items to recipients or carriers and obtain collection evidence.

tasks.design: Configure a delivery register in the {WORKFLOW} with barcode entry, recipient lookup from the {HCM}, collection receipts and automatic notices through the {EMAIL}. A deterministic connector prepares labels in the {OTHER} postal booking system after an operator checks the destination and service. Receiving, sorting, packing and physical handover stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling dominates. A shared register and separate postal interface make small clerical improvements easy to overlook.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, barcode capture and inexpensive connectors can remove duplicate typing and notification work without changing physical handling.
tasks.still_hard: Damaged parcels, illegible labels, confidential items and disputed handovers require physical inspection and judgement. Small delivery volumes may not justify a custom connector.
tasks.human_edge: Maintaining custody, detecting physical problems and deciding how to handle unusual or sensitive deliveries.
tasks.altitude: The operator spends less time logging deliveries and sending collection notices. Physical work and decision rights largely stay the same.

reach.task: Manage uncollected deliveries and secure collection arrangements.
reach.learn: Identity checks, storage limits and custody procedures.

reach.task: Prepare recurring outgoing correspondence for dispatch.
reach.learn: Address validation, dispatch categories and confidential handling.

evidence.claim: Barcode entry, delivery records and rule-based notices can reduce clerical work while physical handling remains manual.
Label preparation can use deterministic field validation and a postal-system connector where an interface is available.
Recipient and collection records require GDPR purpose limitation, restricted access and appropriate retention.

assumptions: Incoming and outgoing deliveries are alternative branches; their time shares describe the combined workload.
The baseline uses a shared spreadsheet for tracked items; ordinary letters may bypass registration.
Automation covers administration, not robotic sorting or packing.
Internal collection uses the same handover step as carrier dispatch.
Effort ranges assume existing devices and a supported postal interface; consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Is there already a delivery register that can be configured?
What proportion of deliveries have readable barcodes?
Does the postal booking system expose a supported interface?
Which items require signatures, identity checks or special storage?
Would collection logs be used to monitor employees, triggering consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Is configuration of an existing register cheaper than a new records app?
Does barcode capture reduce entry time after handling exceptions?
Does dispatch volume justify the connector cost?
new_work: Resolve unmatched recipients and unreadable barcodes.
Maintain recipient locations and collection rules.
Review failed notices and overdue collections.
Maintain postal mappings and delete expired custody records.

tasks.short: Update directories, prepare documents, proofread records and create routine schedules.

steps.what: Receive directory changes, document requests or scheduling instructions.
Check employee names, departments and contact changes against authorised employee records.
Enter verified contact changes into the telephone directory.
Type supplied content into standard document templates.
Proofread the draft against source content and correct errors.

loop.input: Document draft, source content and approved style rules.
loop.check: Check names, dates and numbers deterministically; require operator acceptance of prose changes.
loop.stop: One review pass and one repair pass; unresolved differences return to the requester.
loop.why_not_simpler: Literal comparison catches copying errors but misses contextual grammar and ambiguous wording.

steps.what: Create and publish routine schedules from availability and coverage requirements.

tasks.design: Use structured requests in the {WORKFLOW} and synchronise approved directory fields from the {HCM} into the {TELEPHONY}. Generate routine documents from templates in the {DOCS}, with a bounded proofreading loop proposing changes for acceptance. Configure availability and coverage checks in the {CALENDAR}, retaining supervisor approval for published schedules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Employee records, telephone directories and document templates were maintained separately. Small variations and unclear ownership kept manual copying in place.
tasks.enabler_now: Field mappings, template generation and calendar rules are mature techniques. AI-assisted coding makes small integrations cheaper, while bounded text review helps with contextual proofreading.
tasks.still_hard: An authoritative employee record may still lack a correct extension or preferred display name. Editorial meaning and staffing exceptions need people; employee schedules also depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a plausible but incorrect change and understanding when wording or scheduling affects people.

ambition.what: Pre-publication contact-route checks for new starters and employee moves.

tasks.altitude: The operator shifts from retyping records to resolving contact exceptions and checking documents. Schedule approval remains with the supervisor; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Check that changed contact details reach employee-facing directories.
reach.learn: Field ownership, synchronisation delays and identity-access boundaries.

reach.task: Prepare consistent routine correspondence from approved templates.
reach.learn: Template design, source verification and version control.

evidence.claim: Configured directory lookup supports names and departments, but directory search changes can take up to 24 hours.
Directory synchronisation and template generation can use deterministic processing; proofreading varied prose may need bounded model review.
Employee records require GDPR access controls and data minimisation; employee consultation requirements vary under national rules.

assumptions: Directory updates, document preparation and scheduling are separate request branches.
Time shares describe the combined administrative workload.
Routine documents use supplied content; substantive original drafting is outside this estimate.
The baseline directory is maintained in the telephone system, rather than assuming a separate spreadsheet.
Effort ranges cover a limited set of fields, templates and schedule rules. Consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which source owns extensions, preferred names and department assignments?
Can the telephone directory accept supported updates?
How much document work fits approved templates?
Are schedules meeting calendars or staffing rosters?
Which national scheduling and employee consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Can existing directory synchronisation remove the need for custom code?
Which document errors escape deterministic checks?
How long do verified directory changes take to become searchable?
Can existing scheduling configuration cover the actual coverage rules?
new_work: Resolve conflicting or missing directory fields.
Monitor synchronisation failures and stale entries.
Maintain templates, mappings and coverage rules.
Review suggested text changes and document versions.
Check permissions when employees join, move or leave.

tasks.short: Take orders, book appointments or rooms, and handle incoming and outgoing faxes.

steps.what: Ask for request details and clarify missing information.

loop.input: Spoken request and the approved fields for its request type.
loop.output: Booking or order fields with missing values identified.
loop.check: Validate field types and read back names, dates, quantities and contact details.
loop.stop: One extraction and two clarification attempts; ambiguous or urgent requests go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Natural speech contains corrections and incomplete details. Structured forms bypass the loop.

steps.what: Check appointment availability or meeting-room capacity and equipment.
Confirm the chosen option with the requester and reserve it.
Send booking details, joining instructions and cancellation information.
Enter customer, item, quantity and delivery details as a draft order.
Check commercial terms and release or return the draft order.
Retrieve incoming faxes from the {OTHER} fax service.
Check the destination and send approved documents through the {OTHER} fax service.

tasks.design: Configure booking availability, reservations and confirmations through the {CALENDAR}, {WORKFLOW} and {EMAIL}. A bounded speech loop captures spoken requests, while deterministic validation creates draft orders in the {ERP} for commercial approval. Configure incoming fax filing in the {DOCS} and checked outgoing transmission through the {OTHER} fax service.
tasks.previous_blocker: One reception role bridged several systems, with verbal requests and different approval rules. Configuration alone did not remove repeated entry between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking and fax features handle routine execution. Small connectors and bounded speech extraction can now be built and maintained with less development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial promises, unusual room needs, calendar races and incorrect fax destinations remain costly exceptions. Incoming fax content without a reliable recipient identifier still needs human routing.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding an unusual request and avoiding commitments that exceed delegated authority.

ambition.what: After-hours appointment requests with confirmed slots and a staffed exception queue.

tasks.altitude: The operator handles fewer standard bookings and typed orders, leaving more time for unusual requests and follow-up. Commercial approval stays with the sales coordinator; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Resolve incomplete orders before commercial review.
reach.learn: Item identification, delivery constraints and the limits of delegated promises.

reach.task: Offer suitable alternatives when requested appointments are unavailable.
reach.learn: Capacity rules, cancellation terms and accessible alternatives.

evidence.claim: A documented telephone assistant can book appointments and route calls, including in Dutch.
Validated order drafts and configured fax workflows are feasible deterministic designs; the digest supplies no implementation case for these steps.
Callers interacting with an AI interface require disclosure and applicable synthetic-audio marking.
Automated emergency-call evaluation or dispatch prioritisation is a distinct high-risk use; this design passes urgent requests to a person.

assumptions: Bookings, orders and faxes are alternative branches, not steps in every request.
Time shares describe the combined workload and include the sales coordinator handoff.
Orders remain drafts until commercial approval.
The baseline uses a digital fax service; physical fax equipment would retain scanning and paper handling.
Only faxes with reliable recipient identifiers route automatically; others enter a restricted exception queue.
Effort ranges cover a small set of request types. Consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which booking types can be confirmed without staff approval?
Can the finance system accept draft orders through a supported interface?
Who can approve prices, delivery promises and order release?
How are incoming fax recipients identified today?
Which GDPR basis, retention periods and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing booking configuration cover room and appointment constraints?
How often do spoken requests need human clarification?
Can simultaneous booking attempts be checked atomically?
Which order checks can become deterministic without changing commercial authority?
Would eliminating fax for consenting correspondents cost less than integrating it?
new_work: Review incomplete requests and ambiguous customer or item matches.
Maintain availability, room rules and confirmation templates.
Handle booking conflicts, cancellations and failed transmissions.
Review unidentified incoming faxes in a restricted queue.
Maintain speech disclosure, access controls and retention settings.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward helping callers, resolving coordination exceptions and maintaining reliable contact routes. Physical delivery work remains substantial, and commercial or staffing authority stays with its current approvers.
reach: Receptionist: coordinate accessible attendance and secure delivery collection.
Customer service representative: resolve incomplete requests and orders.
Computer user support specialist: investigate directory and connection failures.
Correspondence clerk: prepare and check routine documents.
skills_to_grow: Directory data quality and basic integration diagnostics.
Booking constraints and commercial escalation boundaries.
Accessible caller support and calm exception handling.
GDPR-aware handling of recordings, documents and delivery records.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an accessible front-door service across calls, appointments and deliveries, with routine execution configured in existing systems and people available for difficult requests.
